text:
ronit: heads-up — noticed a spike in soft-429s from prod canary starting 10:20. correlates with the microbatch change rolled this morning.
kai: saw that too, looks like token_budget_target went from 512 -> 640 in the rollout. saw more kernel fallbacks in the profile.
ashley: linking the flamegraph: https://internal.perf/fg/3568 — nvcc-optimized kernel time doubled for some shards.
ronit: exact failure pattern: higher KV miss rate + larger batch sizes -> some streams exceed preferred sequence length and kernel chooser falls back to fallback_wave_kernel (slower).
maria: do we have the kvcache hit-rate per-admit-window? I bet the larger token budget increased prefix preservation, reducing TTL churn but increasing mismatched seqlen in batches.
perf-bot: automated-alert: 'soft-429-rate' exceeded 0.8% for route /v1/generate on shard gpu-pool-12 between 10:21-10:35.
samir: quick repro on staging: run burst script with N=200 parallel, token_budget_target=640 -> avg latency 210ms -> 429 increase. With token_budget_target=512 -> latency 160ms and 429s almost gone.
kai: interesting. kernel selection heuristic currently uses batch_median_seq_len and kernel_profile map. if one request has much longer seqlen, continuous-batcher currently pads to max_seqlen of the batch, causing heavy kernel mismatch.
ronit: proposal: two changes: 1) cap batch padding by batch_quantile (e.g., 90th pct) and permit slice-out for outliers, 2) add a kvcache-prefetch grace flag that prevents admission of requests if recent kvcache miss ratio > 0.25 for that model.
ashley: pseudo-config sample:
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 512
  max_batch_latency_ms: 18
  padding_quantile: 0.9
  outlier_slice_policy: true
kvcache:
  prefetch_grace_window_ms: 400
  miss_ratio_threshold: 0.25
```
maria: the prefetch grace sounds good but we should be careful — backpressure from kvcache could cause cascade into other shards. maybe implement a soft-probabilistic-defer instead of hard reject. e.g., defer 30% of admits when miss_ratio > threshold.
samir: +1 for probabilistic defer. also add telemetry: mark admits with reason token_budget/kvcache/outlier so we can track which branch is reducing 429s.
kai: also saw perf-regression correlation with the kernel_guided_prefetch flag off. turning it on on staging reduced kernel fallbacks by ~40%. we should try enabling it in the canary and monitor.
ronit: next steps: 1) rollback token_budget_target to 512 on canary now, 2) enable kernel_guided_prefetch on canary, 3) push the padding_quantile change to staging for 24h A/B, 4) implement soft probabilistic kvcache-defer metric + telemetry. i'll open issues.
ashley: can you add a small experiment note in the canary runbook so oncall knows to watch kpi: soft_429_rate, kvcache_miss_ratio, kernel_fallback_rate?
ronit: will do. also adding alert tweak: mute the perf-bot for up to 20m on low-sev transient soft-429 spikes during experiments.
maria: FYI, edge-case: for very short sequences (<16 tokens) padding_quantile can harm throughput. add an exception for short seq batches.
samir: putting a quick harness in CI that fuzzes seq lengths and kvcache_hit flags to guard against regressions.
kai: ok - i'll coordinate the canary rollback + kernel_guided_prefetch flip. pinged infra to reserve extra logging retention. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: action-logged: incident-note created 356800-01, assigned to ronit, kai.
ronit: thanks, team. will post a short postmortem if changes change 429 curve.
ashley: great. :rocket:
